jevBench15.scope: The MIT notice applies to JevBench source code and method documentation. Aggregate results come from Benchmark Heaven's public versioned API. Evaluated model weights, external code, upstream datasets, and other third-party data retain their own terms.

valsAi.scope: Published leaderboard aggregates and evaluation settings only. Dataset contents are not included.

field_notes.overall.score: BenchLM's published overall score (displayScore) in ranking_mode; rank = overallRank. Keep the mode with the score when citing.
field_notes.overall.provisional_score: BenchLM marks this provisional; not used for the published board.
field_notes.category_scores: Verified category scores (falls back to display scores when no verified set exists).
field_notes.scores: Every per-benchmark value BenchLM publishes for the model, in each benchmark's native unit (see benchmarks[].format, lower_is_better).
field_notes.leaderboard: The published rankings exactly as in leaderboard.json (overall + per category).
field_notes.omitted: comparisons.json (precomputed head-to-head pairs) and stats.json (editorial statements) are derived from the data here and left out; price-index.json is included as price_index.

benchmarks.name: Protein Mutation Attribution
benchmarks.description: Anthropic's life-sciences evaluation of whether a model can attribute the effects of protein mutations.
benchmarks.paper_title: Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 system card

benchmarks.name: Protein Domain ID
benchmarks.description: Anthropic's protein-understanding test: from an amino acid sequence alone, choose the correct Pfam domain family among similar distractors, without tools.
benchmarks.paper_title: Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 system card

benchmarks.name: PhysicianBench
benchmarks.description: A public benchmark of 100 physician tasks carried out inside an electronic health record system.
benchmarks.paper_title: Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 system card

benchmarks.name: GaRAGe
benchmarks.description: Amazon benchmark of grounded answers in retrieval-augmented generation, with human labels for which supplied passages are relevant.

benchmarks.name: RAGTruth (provider reports)
benchmarks.description: Corpus of retrieval-augmented responses annotated word by word for unsupported or contradicted content.
benchmarks.tasks: Retrieval-augmented question answering, summarization and data-to-text

benchmarks.name: HealthBench (raw)
benchmarks.description: Raw score on realistic multi-turn healthcare conversations graded against expert-written rubrics.
benchmarks.paper_title: HealthBench: Evaluating Large Language Models Towards Improved Human Health

benchmarks.name: HealthBench (length-adjusted)
benchmarks.description: HealthBench score after applying a verbosity penalty to model responses.
benchmarks.paper_title: HealthBench: Evaluating Large Language Models Towards Improved Human Health

benchmarks.name: HealthBench Professional (raw)
benchmarks.description: Raw score on physician-authored clinical consult, documentation, and research conversations.
benchmarks.paper_title: HealthBench Professional: Evaluating Large Language Models on Real Clinician Chats

benchmarks.name: HealthBench (raw, Artificial Analysis)
benchmarks.description: Artificial Analysis independently evaluates 5,000 conversations and reports a raw rubric score.

benchmarks.name: HealthBench (length-adjusted, Artificial Analysis)
benchmarks.description: Artificial Analysis independently evaluates 5,000 conversations and reports a length-adjusted rubric score.

benchmarks.name: HealthBench Professional (length-adjusted, Artificial Analysis)
benchmarks.full_name: Artificial Analysis HealthBench Professional length-adjusted score
benchmarks.description: Artificial Analysis independently evaluates 525 conversations and reports a length-adjusted rubric score.

benchmarks.name: HealthBench Professional (raw, Artificial Analysis)
benchmarks.full_name: Artificial Analysis HealthBench Professional raw score
benchmarks.description: Artificial Analysis independently evaluates 525 conversations and reports a raw rubric score.

benchmarks.name: BioMysteryBench (human-solvable)
benchmarks.description: Computational biology challenges that independent human experts were able to solve.

benchmarks.name: BioMysteryBench (human-difficult)
benchmarks.description: Computational biology challenges with objective answers that remained unsolved by independent human experts.

benchmarks.name: SpatialBench Verified
benchmarks.description: Analysis of spatial transcriptomics data across externally validated biological problems.

benchmarks.name: SingleCellBench
benchmarks.description: Single-cell RNA sequencing analysis tasks spanning common bioinformatics workflows.

benchmarks.name: ProteinGym Hard
benchmarks.description: Predicts mutation effects by ranking mutant protein sequences against wild type and comparing against laboratory measurements.

benchmarks.name: Protein Design
benchmarks.description: Generates novel protein sequences under family, topology, globularity, and structural-motif constraints.

benchmarks.name: Morphology-to-molecule matching
benchmarks.description: Matches multi-channel cellular imaging data to the molecule-dose perturbations that produced it.

benchmarks.name: Medicinal chemistry
benchmarks.description: Selects compounds with the highest or lowest measured ADME-related property from molecular structures and reference values.

benchmarks.name: Protein Design library ranking
benchmarks.description: Ranks held-out protein designs for experimental testing using wet-lab campaign measurements and a selection objective.

benchmarks.name: De novo protein-binder design
benchmarks.full_name: Anthropic de novo protein-binder design evaluation
benchmarks.description: Designs diverse miniprotein binders against target protein structures in a GPU-equipped research sandbox.

benchmarks.name: Organic chemistry V2
benchmarks.description: Chemistry tasks covering spectroscopy, synthesis planning, reaction prediction, and chemical structure images.

benchmarks.name: Protocols (troubleshooting)
benchmarks.description: Detects and fixes errors in molecular-biology protocols using document, code, and web-search tools.

benchmarks.name: Protocols (understanding)
benchmarks.description: Extends online molecular-biology protocols in additional directions using document and web-search tools.

benchmarks.name: AA Openness Index
benchmarks.description: A display-only Artificial Analysis model-openness index.

benchmarks.name: AA MMLU-Pro
benchmarks.description: An independently evaluated MMLU-Pro result from Artificial Analysis.

benchmarks.name: MMLU
benchmarks.description: A comprehensive multiple-choice question answering test covering 57 tasks including elementary mathematics, US history, computer science, law, and more. Tests knowledge across diverse academic subjects from high school to professional level.
benchmarks.authors: Dan Hendrycks, Collin Burns, Steven Basart, Andy Zou, Mantas Mazeika, Dawn Song, Jacob Steinhardt

benchmarks.name: GPQA
benchmarks.description: A challenging dataset of 448 multiple-choice questions written by domain experts in biology, physics, and chemistry. Designed to be difficult even for skilled non-experts with access to Google.
benchmarks.paper_title: GPQA: A Graduate-Level Google-Proof Q&A Benchmark
benchmarks.authors: David Rein, Betty Li Hou, Asa Cooper Stickland, Jackson Petty, Richard Yuanzhe Pang, Julien Dirani, Julian Michael, Samuel R. Bowman

benchmarks.name: GPQA-D
benchmarks.description: Graduate-level science questions from provider comparison charts and open evaluations.
benchmarks.paper_title: GPQA: A Graduate-Level Google-Proof Q&A Benchmark
benchmarks.authors: David Rein, Betty Li Hou, Asa Cooper Stickland, Jackson Petty, Richard Yuanzhe Pang, Julien Dirani, Julian Michael, Samuel R. Bowman

benchmarks.name: SuperGPQA
benchmarks.full_name: SuperGPQA: Scaling LLM Evaluation Across 285 Graduate Disciplines
benchmarks.description: An expanded version of GPQA that evaluates graduate-level knowledge and reasoning capabilities across 285 disciplines, providing comprehensive coverage of academic domains.
benchmarks.paper_title: SuperGPQA: Scaling LLM Evaluation Across 285 Graduate Disciplines
benchmarks.authors: Xiaoxuan Du, Yao Yao, Kexin Ma, Bowen Wang, Tianyu Zheng, Kaiyan Zhu, Yiming Zhang, Yutao Zhu, Jiawei Zhou, Jingren Zhou

benchmarks.name: MMLU-Pro
benchmarks.description: An enhanced version of MMLU with 10 answer choices instead of 4, featuring more reasoning-focused questions that better differentiate frontier models.
benchmarks.paper_title: MMLU-Pro: A More Robust and Challenging Multi-Task Language Understanding Benchmark
benchmarks.authors: Yubo Wang, Xueguang Ma, Ge Zhang, Yuansheng Ni, Abhranil Chandra, Shiguang Guo, Weiming Ren, Aaran Arulraj, Xuan He, Ziyan Jiang, Tianle Li, Max Ku, Kai Wang, Alex Zhuang, Rongqi Fan, Xiang Yue, Wenhu Chen

benchmarks.name: AGIEval
benchmarks.description: A human-centric exam benchmark for general knowledge and reasoning reported in DeepSeek-V4 base-model evaluations.
benchmarks.tasks: General academic and professional exam questions

benchmarks.name: HLE
benchmarks.description: An expert-authored benchmark designed to probe frontier knowledge and reasoning. BenchLM keeps protocol differences visible because tool-assisted and closed-book HLE runs answer different questions.
benchmarks.authors: Center for AI Safety, Scale AI, and thousands of expert contributors

benchmarks.name: HLE-Diamond
benchmarks.description: Accuracy on the 1,000-question HLE-Diamond set without tools, using the benchmark owner's high-reasoning evaluation.
benchmarks.authors: Center for AI Safety and Scale AI

benchmarks.name: HLE-Diamond (highest effort)
benchmarks.full_name: Humanity's Last Exam Diamond without tools at highest reasoning effort
benchmarks.description: Accuracy on the 1,000-question HLE-Diamond set without tools at each model's highest available reasoning effort.
benchmarks.format: Accuracy without tools, highest available reasoning effort
benchmarks.authors: Center for AI Safety and Scale AI

benchmarks.name: HLE-Diamond (web+code)
benchmarks.full_name: Humanity's Last Exam Diamond with web and code tools
benchmarks.description: Accuracy on HLE-Diamond with constrained web search, page fetching, and code execution at high reasoning effort.
benchmarks.tasks: 1,000 expert questions with web and code tools
benchmarks.format: Accuracy with web and code, reasoning high
benchmarks.authors: Center for AI Safety and Scale AI

benchmarks.name: HLE-Verified
benchmarks.description: A verified and revised Humanity's Last Exam set that removes uncertain items and repairs fixable questions before evaluating frontier expert reasoning.
benchmarks.paper_title: HLE-Verified: A Systematic Verification and Structured Revision of Humanity's Last Exam
benchmarks.authors: Weiqi Zhai, Zhihai Wang, Jinghang Wang, Boyu Yang, Xiaogang Li, Xiang Xu, Bohan Wang, Peng Wang, Xingzhe Wu, Anfeng Li, Qiyuan Feng, Yuhao Zhou, Shoulin Han, Wenjie Luo, Yiyuan Li, Yaxuan Wang, Ruixian Luo, Guojie Lin, Peiyao Xiao, Chengliang Xu, Ben Wang, Zeyu Wang, Zichao Chen, Jianan Ye, Yijie Hu, Jialong Chen, Zongwen Shen, Yuliang Xu, An Yang, Bowen Yu, Dayiheng Liu, Junyang Lin, Hu Wei, Que Shen, Bing Zhao

benchmarks.name: LABBench2
benchmarks.full_name: LABBench2: An Improved Benchmark for AI Systems Performing Biology Research
benchmarks.description: A benchmark of realistic biology-research tasks involving literature, figures, tables, databases, and bioinformatics files.
benchmarks.paper_title: LABBench2: An Improved Benchmark for AI Systems Performing Biology Research
benchmarks.authors: Jon M. Laurent, Albert Bou, Michael Pieler, Conor Igoe, Alex Andonian, Siddharth Narayanan, James Braza, Alexandros Sanchez Vassopoulos, Jacob L. Steenwyk, Blake Lash, Andrew D. White, Samuel G. Rodriques

benchmarks.name: FrontierScience
benchmarks.description: A benchmark for research-level scientific reasoning, designed to separate frontier models on difficult science tasks that mix domain knowledge with deep reasoning.

benchmarks.name: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index
benchmarks.description: Artificial Analysis describes itself as an independent AI benchmarking company. Its Intelligence Index combines the company's own evaluations of AI models into one score per model. BenchLM compiles reported index scores, which can come from different index versions, and shows them for reference only.

benchmarks.name: AA-GPQA Diamond
benchmarks.description: An Artificial Analysis GPQA Diamond score.
benchmarks.paper_title: Artificial Analysis GPQA Diamond Benchmark Leaderboard

benchmarks.name: AA-HLE
benchmarks.description: An Artificial Analysis Humanity's Last Exam score.
benchmarks.paper_title: Artificial Analysis Humanity's Last Exam Benchmark Leaderboard

benchmarks.name: AA-Omniscience Index
benchmarks.description: A display-only Artificial Analysis factual knowledge index.

benchmarks.name: AA-Omniscience Accuracy
benchmarks.description: An Artificial Analysis knowledge metric for the proportion of correctly answered questions.

benchmarks.name: AA-Omniscience Hallucination Rate
benchmarks.description: A display-only Artificial Analysis factuality metric for the rate of incorrect answers among non-correct responses.

benchmarks.name: Kimi Hallu Bench
benchmarks.description: Moonshot AI's internal factuality benchmark built from challenging, de-identified prompts drawn from practical work tasks, scored as the claim-level hallucination rate.
benchmarks.paper_title: Kimi K3.1 Pro Tech Blog: Advancing Open Intelligence

benchmarks.name: SimpleQA
benchmarks.full_name: Measuring Short-Form Factuality in Large Language Models
benchmarks.description: A benchmark that evaluates the ability of language models to answer short, fact-seeking questions accurately. Focuses on factual correctness rather than reasoning complexity.
benchmarks.paper_title: Measuring short-form factuality in large language models
benchmarks.authors: Jason Wei, Najoung Kim, Hyung Won Chung, Yu-An Chung, Siddhartha Papay, Yifeng Lu, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Luke Zettlemoyer

benchmarks.name: Chinese-SimpleQA
benchmarks.description: A Chinese short-form factuality benchmark reported by DeepSeek for V4 model evaluations.

benchmarks.name: OpenBookQA
benchmarks.description: A science question-answering benchmark that tests whether models can apply a small open-book set of elementary science facts to multi-step reasoning questions.
benchmarks.paper_title: Can a Suit of Armor Conduct Electricity? A New Dataset for Open Book Question Answering
benchmarks.authors: Todor Mihaylov, Peter Clark, Tushar Khot, Ashish Sabharwal

benchmarks.name: HealthBench Hard
benchmarks.description: A harder subset of OpenAI's HealthBench for evaluating open-ended medical and health reasoning with rubric-based grading.

benchmarks.name: HealthBench Professional
benchmarks.description: An open benchmark for clinician-facing model responses across care consult, writing and documentation, and medical research tasks.
benchmarks.paper_title: HealthBench Professional: Evaluating Large Language Models on Real Clinician Chats
benchmarks.authors: Rebecca Soskin Hicks, Mikhail Trofimov, Dominick Lim, Rahul K. Arora, Foivos Tsimpourlas, Preston Bowman, Michael Sharman, Chi Tong, Kavin Karthik, Arnav Dugar, Akshay Jagadeesh, Khaled Saab, Johannes Heidecke, Ashley Alexander, Nate Gross, Karan Singhal

benchmarks.name: MedXpertQA (Text)
benchmarks.description: A medical multiple-choice benchmark spanning many specialties with 10 answer options per question.

benchmarks.name: FrontierScience Research
benchmarks.description: A research-focused FrontierScience evaluation variant for scientific investigation and problem solving.

benchmarks.name: TruthfulQA
benchmarks.description: A benchmark designed to measure whether language models produce truthful answers instead of repeating common misconceptions or misleading falsehoods.
benchmarks.paper_title: TruthfulQA: Measuring How Models Mimic Human Falsehoods
benchmarks.authors: Stephanie Lin, Jacob Hilton, Owain Evans

benchmarks.name: HLE w/o tools
benchmarks.description: Tool-free variant of Humanity's Last Exam that isolates a model's raw frontier reasoning.

benchmarks.name: MMLU-Pro (Arcee)
benchmarks.description: A display-only MMLU-Pro reference from Arcee AI's Trinity-Large-Thinking launch chart.
benchmarks.paper_title: Trinity-Large-Thinking: Scaling an Open Source Frontier Agent

benchmarks.name: MMLU-Redux
benchmarks.description: A harder refresh of MMLU intended to keep broad knowledge evaluation useful after the original benchmark became too easy for frontier models.

benchmarks.name: MMMLU
benchmarks.description: A multilingual MMLU-style benchmark reported in provider evaluation tables.

benchmarks.name: C-Eval
benchmarks.description: A Chinese-language academic and professional benchmark spanning humanities, social science, STEM, and applied subjects.
benchmarks.paper_title: C-Eval: A Multi-Level Multi-Discipline Chinese Evaluation Suite for Foundation Models

benchmarks.name: CMMLU
benchmarks.description: A Chinese multitask academic benchmark reported in DeepSeek-V4 base-model evaluations.

benchmarks.name: MultiLoKo
benchmarks.description: A multilingual/localized knowledge benchmark reported in DeepSeek-V4 base-model evaluations.

benchmarks.name: FACTS Parametric
benchmarks.description: A parametric factuality benchmark reported in DeepSeek-V4 base-model evaluations.

benchmarks.name: TriviaQA
benchmarks.description: A reading and trivia question-answering benchmark reported in DeepSeek-V4 base-model evaluations.

benchmarks.name: FinanceArena
benchmarks.description: An AfterQuery benchmark of open-ended financial analysis that requires models to read financial data, make assumptions, and return exact answers.
benchmarks.format: Open-ended financial QA with exact-match grading

benchmarks.name: GPQA Diamond (Vals)
benchmarks.description: Vals AI’s independent run of the GPQA Diamond graduate-level science questions.
benchmarks.paper_title: Vals AI GPQA Diamond, Vals AI run leaderboard

benchmarks.name: MMLU-Pro (Vals)
benchmarks.description: Vals AI’s independent run of MMLU-Pro across fourteen academic subjects.
benchmarks.paper_title: Vals AI MMLU-Pro, Vals AI run leaderboard

benchmarks.name: PostTrainBench v1.1
benchmarks.description: Post-training four base language models across seven weighted benchmarks, with ten hours and one H100 per run.
benchmarks.tasks: Post-training Qwen3 1.7B and 4B, SmolLM3 3B, and Gemma3 4B
benchmarks.format: Weighted aggregate across four base models and seven benchmarks

benchmarks.name: PostTrainBench v1
benchmarks.description: The first seven-benchmark PostTrainBench board, kept by the source as an archived version.
benchmarks.tasks: Post-training four base models on seven benchmarks
benchmarks.format: Weighted aggregate across four base models and seven benchmarks
benchmarks.authors: Ben Rank, Hardik Bhatnagar, Matthias Bethge, Maksym Andriushchenko and the PostTrainBench team

benchmarks.name: ProgramBench (episode 1)
benchmarks.full_name: ProgramBench hidden-test pass rate after episode 1
benchmarks.description: Program-reconstruction hidden-test pass rate after the first of five sequential long-context episodes.
benchmarks.paper_title: ProgramBench: Can language models rebuild programs from scratch?

benchmarks.name: AA LiveCodeBench
benchmarks.description: An independently evaluated LiveCodeBench result from Artificial Analysis.

benchmarks.name: AA Terminal-Bench 2.1
benchmarks.description: An independently evaluated Terminal-Bench v2.1 result from Artificial Analysis.
benchmarks.paper_title: Artificial Analysis Terminal-Bench v2.1 Benchmark Leaderboard

benchmarks.name: Terminal-Bench 2.1
benchmarks.description: Terminal-Bench 2.1 results, mostly provider-reported, stored separately from the Terminal-Bench 2.0 lane.

benchmarks.name: HumanEval
benchmarks.full_name: Evaluating Large Language Models Trained on Code
benchmarks.description: HumanEval tests whether generated Python functions pass unit tests on 164 handwritten problems. These scores describe function-level correctness; they do not measure repository work or a coding agent.
benchmarks.paper_title: Evaluating Large Language Models Trained on Code
benchmarks.authors: Mark Chen, Jerry Tworek, Heewoo Jun, Qiming Yuan, Henrique Ponde de Oliveira Pinto, Jared Kaplan, Harri Edwards, Yuri Burda, Nicholas Joseph, Greg Brockman, Alex Ray, Raul Puri, Gretchen Krueger, Michael Petrov, Heidy Khlaaf, Girish Sastry, Pamela Mishkin, Brooke Chan, Scott Gray, Nick Ryder, Mikhail Pavlov, Alethea Power, Lukasz Kaiser, Mohammad Bavarian, Clemens Winter, Philippe Tillet, Felipe Petroski Such, Dave Cummings, Matthias Plappert, Fotios Chantzis, Elizabeth Barnes, Ariel Herbert-Voss, William Hebgen Guss, Alex Nichol, Alex Paino, Nikolas Tezak, Jie Tang, Igor Babuschkin, Suchir Balaji, Shantanu Jain, William Saunders, Christopher Hesse, Andrew N. Carr, Jan Leike, Josh Achiam, Vedant Misra, Evan Morikawa, Alec Radford, Matthew Knight, Miles Brundage, Mira Murati, Katie Mayer, Peter Welinder, Bob McGrew, Dario Amodei, Sam McCandlish, Ilya Sutskever, Wojciech Zaremba

benchmarks.name: BigCodeBench
benchmarks.description: A code-generation benchmark reported in DeepSeek-V4 base-model evaluations.

benchmarks.name: Codeforces
benchmarks.description: Competitive-programming rating reported for DeepSeek-V4 thinking-mode evaluations.

benchmarks.name: Terminal-Bench 2.0
benchmarks.description: A benchmark for agentic software engineering tasks executed in real terminal environments. DeepSeek reports it in the agentic section, while BenchLM also mirrors it in coding for models that publish it as a developer-task signal.

benchmarks.name: SWE-bench Verified
benchmarks.description: SWE-bench Verified tests patches for 500 human-filtered GitHub issues. A score measures how many tasks an evaluated model-and-agent setup resolved; the model name alone does not identify that setup.
benchmarks.paper_title: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?
benchmarks.authors: Carlos E. Jimenez, John Yang, Alexander Wettig, Shunyu Yao, Kexin Pei, Ofir Press, Karthik Narasimhan

benchmarks.name: SWE-Rebench
benchmarks.description: A continuously updated software engineering benchmark by Nebius using fresh GitHub issues to avoid contamination. Models are evaluated 5 times per problem under a fixed ReAct scaffolding; the Resolved Rate (best pass@1) is reported.
benchmarks.paper_title: SWE-Rebench: Contamination-Free Evaluation of Software Engineering Agents

benchmarks.name: LiveCodeBench
benchmarks.full_name: LiveCodeBench: Holistic and Contamination Free Evaluation of Large Language Models for Code
benchmarks.description: A continuously updated coding benchmark built from newly collected LeetCode, AtCoder, and Codeforces problems. Fresh problem windows reduce one contamination path, but results still need a release and setup check.
benchmarks.paper_title: LiveCodeBench: Holistic and Contamination Free Evaluation of Large Language Models for Code
benchmarks.authors: Naman Jain, King Han, Alex Gu, Wen-Ding Li, Fanjia Yan, Tianjun Zhang, Sida Wang, Armando Solar-Lezama, Koushik Sen, Ion Stoica

benchmarks.name: LiveCodeBench v6
benchmarks.description: LiveCodeBench v6 is a named release slice used in provider comparison tables. Keeping it separate prevents v6 results from being mixed into older or rolling LiveCodeBench windows.
benchmarks.paper_title: LiveCodeBench official repository and release documentation

benchmarks.name: LiveCodeBench v5
benchmarks.description: LiveCodeBench v5 is a named release and date-window slice. BenchLM keeps explicitly labeled v5 rows outside the rolling weighted lane.
benchmarks.paper_title: LiveCodeBench official repository and release documentation

benchmarks.name: LiveCodeBench Pass@1-COT
benchmarks.description: This lane contains DeepSeek's LiveCodeBench Pass@1-COT results. The explicit metric and prompting label keeps them separate from generic and version-specific LiveCodeBench rows.

benchmarks.name: LiveCodeBench Pro
benchmarks.description: A harder competitive-programming benchmark family built from Codeforces, ICPC, and IOI problems, with quarter-specific public leaderboards and difficulty-aware reporting.
benchmarks.paper_title: LiveCodeBench Pro: How Do Olympiad Medalists Judge LLMs in Competitive Programming?

benchmarks.name: FLTEval
benchmarks.description: A repository-level Lean 4 proof engineering benchmark that measures whether a model can complete formal proofs and correctly define new mathematical concepts inside realistic FLT project pull requests.
benchmarks.paper_title: Leanstral: Open-Source foundation for trustworthy vibe-coding

benchmarks.name: SWE-bench Pro
benchmarks.description: A long-horizon repository benchmark built to test realistic software engineering work. Its scores need a task-quality and setup check before they support a coding-agent decision.
benchmarks.paper_title: SWE-Bench Pro: Can AI Agents Solve Long-Horizon Software Engineering Tasks?
benchmarks.authors: Xiang Deng, Jeff Da, Edwin Pan, Yannis Yiming He, Charles Ide, Kanak Garg, Niklas Lauffer, Andrew Park, Nitin Pasari, Chetan Rane, Karmini Sampath, Maya Krishnan, Srivatsa Kundurthy, Sean Hendryx, Zifan Wang, Chen Bo Calvin Zhang, Noah Jacobson, Bing Liu, Brad Kenstler

benchmarks.name: Senior SWE-Bench
benchmarks.description: A Snorkel AI benchmark of senior-level software engineering tasks emphasizing under-specified feature work, bug/performance investigation, and taste-based correctness.

benchmarks.name: VulcanBench Frontier v4
benchmarks.description: An open coding benchmark of 23 hard behavioural-reconstruction tasks, run at every reasoning-effort level and scored on correctness and judged code quality.
benchmarks.format: Combined score (correctness and judged code quality), best effort per model

benchmarks.name: VulcanBench v3
benchmarks.description: An open software-engineering benchmark built from real merged post-cutoff pull requests across Python, Rust, TypeScript, JavaScript, and Go repositories. Replaced by VulcanBench Frontier v4 in September 2026.
benchmarks.tasks: 23 post-cutoff repository tasks in the v3 report
benchmarks.format: Pass@1 with low, medium, and high effort

benchmarks.name: OpenHarmony Bench v1.2
benchmarks.description: An app-level coding benchmark that asks DevEco Code configurations to build, extend, fix and migrate buildable OpenHarmony ArkTS applications.
benchmarks.tasks: App-development, bug-fix and migration tasks (count not published)
benchmarks.difficulty: End-to-end OpenHarmony application development and migration
benchmarks.paper_title: OpenHarmony Bench: Evaluating LLMs and Coding Agents on OpenHarmony App Development

benchmarks.name: OpenHarmony Bench v1.0
benchmarks.description: An app-level coding benchmark that asks DevEco Code configurations to implement observable behavior in buildable OpenHarmony ArkTS applications. Replaced by OpenHarmony Bench v1.2 in November 2026.
benchmarks.paper_title: OpenHarmony Bench: Evaluating LLMs and Coding Agents on OpenHarmony App Development

benchmarks.name: VulcanBench CII v1
benchmarks.description: A post-cutoff software-engineering benchmark with hidden functional tests and regression guards, reported for vendor coding-agent harnesses.

benchmarks.name: FrontierCode 1.1 Main
benchmarks.description: Cognition's 100-task software-engineering benchmark for whether coding agents produce mergeable, production-quality pull requests, scored for correctness, tests, scope, style, and maintainability through maintainer-authored rubrics.
benchmarks.format: Repository task completion with maintainer rubrics

benchmarks.name: FrontierCode 1.1 Extended
benchmarks.description: Cognition's 150-task Extended subset of the FrontierCode 1.1 software-engineering benchmark.
benchmarks.format: Repository task completion with maintainer rubrics

benchmarks.name: FrontierCode 2.0 (AA)
benchmarks.description: Artificial Analysis's own run of Cognition's FrontierCode 2.0 coding-agent benchmark, one of the nine evaluations in its Intelligence Index v5, judged on whether each pull request is mergeable.
benchmarks.format: Weighted rubric score with blocking criteria

benchmarks.name: Aikido Arena
benchmarks.description: Aikido Security's live benchmark of how well AI models rediscover real vulnerabilities. Each model runs three times on 32 recently disclosed CVEs in open-source repositories, and the score is the share it finds in at least one run (pass@3 recall).
benchmarks.tasks: 32 recently disclosed CVEs in real open-source repositories
benchmarks.format: Three runs per model in Aikido's code-analysis harness (30 turns, no internet)
benchmarks.difficulty: Rediscovering real vulnerabilities from source, including missing checks and long call chains

benchmarks.tasks: 26 known CVEs from the GitHub advisory database
benchmarks.format: Three runs per model and reasoning level in Aikido's code-analysis harness
benchmarks.difficulty: Rediscovering known vulnerabilities with the investigator pointed at the vulnerable code
benchmarks.paper_title: Benchmarking 13 AI models on rediscovering known CVEs

benchmarks.name: FrontierMemory
benchmarks.full_name: FrontierMemory: benchmarking continual learning through memory
benchmarks.description: Letta's benchmark of how good the memory is that an AI model writes from past agent work. The model studies a corpus of earlier agent transcripts and writes memory files; the score is the share of 15 memory-dependent coding and knowledge-work tasks that a task agent then fully passes with that memory, averaged over three runs.
benchmarks.tasks: 15 memory-dependent coding and knowledge-work tasks adapted from DeepSWE, SkillsBench, AutomationBench, APEX-Agents and EnterpriseOps-Gym
benchmarks.format: Memory written from a corpus of past agent transcripts in Letta Dream (6-hour limit, no internet), then used by a task agent in Letta Code; three runs
benchmarks.difficulty: Learning task conventions, user preferences and environment facts from past transcripts that the task prompt leaves out
benchmarks.paper_title: FrontierMemory 1.0: Benchmarking continual learning through memory

benchmarks.name: FrontierMemory 1.0
benchmarks.description: The first FrontierMemory table from Letta's launch post: 7 memory models on 15 memory-dependent tasks, scored by full-pass rate over three runs, on the first transcript corpus.
benchmarks.format: Memory written in Letta Dream from the first transcript corpus, used by a task agent in Letta Code; three runs
benchmarks.difficulty: Learning task, user and environment memory from past agent transcripts
benchmarks.paper_title: FrontierMemory 1.0: Benchmarking continual learning through memory

benchmarks.name: OpenWorldEngineer-Bench
benchmarks.description: Mercor's benchmark of AI agents on 26 long, open-ended engineering tasks in science, software, ML and engineering, built by domain experts. Each model makes 8 attempts per task, of 4 to 18 hours each, and the score is the mean task score on a scale from the starting point (0) to the best result the task allows (100).
benchmarks.tasks: 26 expert-built engineering tasks in 4 domains (science, software, ML, engineering)
benchmarks.format: 8 attempts per task in the Harbor agent harness, 4 to 18 hours each, web search over an October 1, 2026 copy of the web
benchmarks.difficulty: Long-horizon engineering work: kernels, data systems, scientific forecasting, CAD and structural and aircraft design

benchmarks.name: FrontierBioML
benchmarks.full_name: FrontierBioML: Evaluating agents on machine learning tasks in computational biology
benchmarks.description: Valen Labs' benchmark of AI agents doing machine learning work in computational biology: 25 tasks in antibody development, designed binders, protein engineering, structural biology and functional genomics. Each agent builds a model from experimental data in an offline sandbox, and its prediction script is scored on held-out measurements, from 0 (a simple baseline) to 100 (a perfect answer), over three runs per task.
benchmarks.tasks: 25 machine learning tasks in computational biology across antibodies, designed binders, protein engineering, structural biology and functional genomics
benchmarks.format: Offline agent sandbox (4 to 32 CPUs, no GPU, about 6 hours); the submitted prediction script runs twice on held-out data; 3 runs per task, 75 per model
benchmarks.difficulty: Building and validating models on messy biological data that generalize to held-out antigens, families, cell types and targets
benchmarks.paper_title: FrontierBioML: Evaluating agents on machine learning tasks in computational biology
benchmarks.authors: Asriel Han, Dominik Scherm, Rohit Rustagi, Ibrahim Abusharkh (Valen Labs)

benchmarks.name: EyeBench
benchmarks.full_name: EyeBench v3: a vision exam for frontier models
benchmarks.description: Adonis Singh's visual reasoning benchmark: 100 generated images, each with one question whose answer is a single number. Models count the differences between two nearly identical panels, count closed loops in a tangle of curves, count the connected parts of a graph drawing, pick the tile that completes a 4x4 pattern, and count the turns along a maze path. Scoring is exact match.
benchmarks.tasks: 100 generated images in five task types: spot the difference, closed loops, graph components, 4x4 pattern completion and maze turns (20 each)
benchmarks.format: One image and one question per request; the answer is a single integer
benchmarks.difficulty: Counting and tracing fine visual detail exactly: small differences between panels, crossing curves and long maze paths
benchmarks.paper_title: EyeBench v3: a vision exam for frontier models

benchmarks.name: OpenWorldEngineer DBF Aircraft
benchmarks.description: One OpenWorldEngineer-Bench task: redesign a small electric aircraft, mechanisms included, for timed laps, heavy cargo and precision drops, measuring it only through a limited budget of tests. Mean of 8 attempts, from the starting design (0) to a perfect reward (100).
benchmarks.format: 8 attempts per model, 8 hours each, private grader
benchmarks.difficulty: Closing an aircraft design across structure, gear, aerodynamics and propulsion from noisy, budgeted tests

benchmarks.name: Company Agent Bench
benchmarks.description: Concept's benchmark of how well an AI agent understands the company it works in. Agents answer 205 questions drawn from one month of Concept's own Slack history: who wrote a message, who was tagged and who sent each reply. The score is overall accuracy.
benchmarks.tasks: 205 questions from one month of Concept's Slack: 100 Authorship, 50 Mentions and 55 Reply matching panels
benchmarks.format: Replay of the Slack history in sandbox workspaces; agent products at default settings, API models in a shared Slack harness
benchmarks.difficulty: Knowing who owns what, who works with whom and how each teammate thinks, from Slack alone

benchmarks.name: BARC-Bench
benchmarks.description: Scale AI's benchmark of whether AI agents stay safe while carrying out ordinary workplace requests. Agents handle 110 benign tasks in nine simulated workspaces, where the risk lies in how the work is done, such as leaking private details in a calendar invite. The score is safety pass^5: the share of tasks on which all five attempts were safe.
benchmarks.tasks: 110 benign workplace requests across nine simulated workspaces: 70 communication tasks, 34 file operations and 6 workspace application changes
benchmarks.format: Agent runs in simulated workspaces with MCP tools; five attempts per task, judged by GPT-5.6 Sol against each task's rubric
benchmarks.difficulty: Respecting boundaries the requester never stated, from workspace records and social norms
benchmarks.authors: Kangkang Li, Kelvin Luu, Lily Ma, Tu Trinh, Ying Liu and Mohamed Elfeki (Scale AI)

benchmarks.name: SWT-bench Verified
benchmarks.full_name: SWT-bench Verified: writing tests that reproduce real GitHub issues
benchmarks.description: A test generation benchmark from LogicStar AI and ETH Zurich's SRI Lab. For each of 433 real GitHub issues from SWE-bench Verified, an agent writes a test that reproduces the reported bug: the test has to fail on the original code and pass once the issue's fix is applied. The score is the share of issues reproduced this way.
benchmarks.tasks: 433 human-verified GitHub issues from SWE-bench Verified (Python repositories); SWT-bench Lite has 276 issues from SWE-bench Lite
benchmarks.format: Agent or model gets the issue and the pre-fix repository and adds tests; tests run before and after the reference fix
benchmarks.difficulty: Reproducing a bug from an issue report as a failing test inside a real project's test suite
benchmarks.paper_title: SWT-Bench: Testing and Validating Real-World Bug-Fixes with Code Agents
benchmarks.authors: Niels Mündler, Mark Niklas Müller, Jingxuan He and Martin Vechev (ETH Zurich, LogicStar AI)

benchmarks.name: SWT-bench Lite
benchmarks.full_name: SWT-bench Lite (276 issues from SWE-bench Lite)
benchmarks.description: The smaller SWT-bench split: 276 GitHub issues from SWE-bench Lite, scored the same way as Verified by the share of issues whose generated tests fail on the original code and pass after the fix.
benchmarks.tasks: 276 GitHub issues from SWE-bench Lite (Python repositories)
benchmarks.format: Agent or model gets the issue and the pre-fix repository and adds tests; tests run before and after the reference fix
benchmarks.difficulty: Reproducing a bug from an issue report as a failing test
benchmarks.paper_title: SWT-Bench: Testing and Validating Real-World Bug-Fixes with Code Agents
benchmarks.authors: Niels Mündler, Mark Niklas Müller, Jingxuan He and Martin Vechev (ETH Zurich, LogicStar AI)

benchmarks.description: Kaggle's Landmark Arena has models build 20 famous landmarks, including the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World, as single-page three.js web apps, and people vote for the better scene.
benchmarks.tasks: 20 famous landmarks built as three.js web pages, rated by human votes
benchmarks.format: Relative rating fitted to human pairwise votes

benchmarks.name: ASCII Arena
benchmarks.description: Kaggle's ASCII Arena asks models to draw everyday subjects as ASCII art, and people vote for the better drawing.
benchmarks.tasks: ASCII drawings of subjects from Google's Quick, Draw! dataset, rated by human votes
benchmarks.format: Relative rating fitted to human pairwise votes

benchmarks.name: FACTS Parametric (Kaggle board)
benchmarks.description: FACTS Parametric asks hard factoid questions from real Google searches and checks whether a model answers them from memory, without tools. It is the parametric-knowledge part of the FACTS suite.
benchmarks.tasks: 2,104 factoid questions: 1,102 public and 1,102 held out

benchmarks.name: Game Arena Go
benchmarks.description: Kaggle Game Arena's Go board ranks models by head-to-head games of Go on a 13 by 13 board.
benchmarks.tasks: Head-to-head Go games on a 13 x 13 board

benchmarks.name: AgenticRL-Bench
benchmarks.description: Eigent AI's AgenticRL-Bench asks coding agents to do real engineering work on reinforcement-learning training stacks: diagnose and fix incidents, upgrade libraries without changing what a training step means, and run live GPU jobs. Kaggle runs the board itself.
benchmarks.tasks: 19 verifiable agentic-RL engineering tasks, three attempts each
benchmarks.format: All-or-nothing hidden checks in a sandbox; pass rate over 57 runs

benchmarks.name: Humanity's First Exam (HFE)
benchmarks.description: Google DeepMind's Humanity's First Exam (HFE) gives frontier models tasks people get right almost every time, like counting objects in a picture or spotting a false premise. The score falls fast when a model that can solve a task doesn't solve it every time.
benchmarks.tasks: 544 prompts in 136 families of four, each run six times
benchmarks.format: Single turn, no tools; a judge marks each final answer right or wrong
benchmarks.difficulty: Easy for people: 3 of 4 raters solved each seed, median 1.5 minutes

benchmarks.name: ShellBench
benchmarks.description: The OpenClaw Foundation's ShellBench tests whether an AI agent can finish the everyday requests people hand to an assistant, working from a folder of that person's own files. A task passes only if the answer meets every correctness and safety criterion, so a right answer that leaks a private detail fails.
benchmarks.tasks: 100 everyday assistant requests, three runs each
benchmarks.format: Agent works in a container of the person's files; all-or-nothing on correctness and safety
benchmarks.difficulty: Everyday requests over a median of 188 files, with outdated records and phishing emails mixed in

benchmarks.name: Dynamic Social Cognition Benchmark
benchmarks.description: Mina Nageh's Kaggle community benchmark "A Dynamic Benchmark for Social Cognition in AGI" has nine tasks on social cognition: understanding emotions, modeling the self and other people, reading intent and tone, and holding to constraints under social pressure.
benchmarks.tasks: Nine social-cognition tasks with written scenarios
benchmarks.format: Raw task scores, one column per task

benchmarks.name: BabaIsBench
benchmarks.full_name: BabaIsBench (Baba Is You intro levels, pass@1)
benchmarks.description: Quesma's BabaIsBench has LLM agents play the puzzle game Baba Is You through a text interface, where a level is won by pushing word tiles around to rewrite its rules. The score here is the first-attempt pass rate on the eight intro levels.
benchmarks.tasks: 8 intro levels of Baba Is You, three attempts per level (Stage 0); 15 further levels run once (Stage 1)
benchmarks.format: Agent plays through a text interface in the Harbor framework
benchmarks.difficulty: Rule-rewriting puzzles that need planning over many moves
benchmarks.paper_title: Baba Is Solved by Fable 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol, but at what cost? (Quesma)

benchmarks.name: BinaryAudit
benchmarks.description: Quesma's BinaryAudit asks AI agents to find backdoors and timebombs planted in compiled, stripped binaries of real server software, using the reverse engineering tools Ghidra and radare2. The score here is the share of detection runs that found the planted code.
benchmarks.tasks: 19 backdoor and timebomb detection tasks on stripped binaries, three runs each (57 runs); 6 tooling and 8 clean-binary tasks reported alongside
benchmarks.format: Agent with Ghidra and radare2 in a terminal, Harbor framework
benchmarks.difficulty: Reverse engineering without source code or symbols
benchmarks.paper_title: We hid backdoors in ~40 MB binaries and asked AI + Ghidra to find them (Quesma)
benchmarks.authors: Piotr Grabowski, Rafał Strzaliński, Michał Kowalczyk, Piotr Migdał, Jacek Migdal (Quesma)

benchmarks.name: OTelBench
benchmarks.description: Quesma's OTelBench asks coding agents to add OpenTelemetry tracing, metrics and logging to small existing services in 11 programming languages. The score is the share of runs where the service then emits correct telemetry.
benchmarks.tasks: 23 OpenTelemetry instrumentation tasks in 11 languages, three attempts each (69 runs)
benchmarks.format: Agent edits a service in a Linux terminal, Harbor framework
benchmarks.difficulty: Distributed tracing and context propagation across services
benchmarks.paper_title: Benchmarking OpenTelemetry: can AI trace your failed login? (Quesma)
benchmarks.authors: Przemek Delewski, Rafał Strzaliński, Piotr Migdał, Jacek Migdal (Quesma)

benchmarks.name: CompileBench
benchmarks.full_name: CompileBench (building real projects from source, pass@1)
benchmarks.description: Quesma's CompileBench hands an agent the unmodified source of an open-source project such as curl, jq or GNU coreutils and asks for a working binary. Tasks include static and musl builds, cross-compiling to Windows and ARM64, and reviving code from 2003.
benchmarks.tasks: 15 build tasks on cowsay, jq, GNU coreutils and curl, three attempts each (45 attempts)
benchmarks.format: Agent in a Docker Linux terminal builds a project from source; the binary is checked
benchmarks.difficulty: Dependency resolution, legacy toolchains, static linking and cross-compilation

benchmarks.name: NYT Connections
benchmarks.description: Lech Mazur's NYT Connections benchmark gives a model 940 puzzles from the New York Times word game, each with up to four extra trick words, and asks it to sort the words into four groups of four in one try. It tests word knowledge, wordplay and resisting plausible decoys.
benchmarks.tasks: 940 NYT Connections puzzles, each with up to four added trick words
benchmarks.format: Sort 16 to 20 words into four groups of four, one attempt per puzzle, no feedback
benchmarks.difficulty: Wordplay, word knowledge and decoys that fit almost-but-not-quite
benchmarks.paper_title: NYT Connections LLM Benchmark (Lech Mazur, GitHub)

benchmarks.name: StealthMark
benchmarks.description: StealthMark, from Stealth Models, scores a model out of 100 on eight original tasks: four on physical reasoning and multi-step planning, and four on producing a precise picture from a brief. The exact instructions are kept private so models can't be tuned to them.
benchmarks.tasks: 8 original tasks: Newton's Mirror, Ground Truth, Latch, Foresight, Mona Lisa, Selfie, Beach and Raccoon
benchmarks.format: Private instructions, blind judging, rendered references and playable game levels
benchmarks.difficulty: Chained physical reasoning, planning without tools and precise visual construction
benchmarks.paper_title: StealthMark: The AI Benchmark Explained (Stealth Models)

benchmarks.name: FrontierPhysics
benchmarks.full_name: End-to-End Physics Research Benchmark for AI Agents
benchmarks.description: FrontierPhysics, from BenchFlow, gives an AI agent a research project written by a working physicist and checks whether it gets the physics right and writes it up well enough to publish. It has 56 tasks across nine fields of physics, and each one is run three times.
benchmarks.tasks: 56 research projects from 42 physicists across nine fields, three trials each (168 rollouts per setup)
benchmarks.format: Agentic research in a sandbox: literature review, simulation or measurement, structured results and a written paper
benchmarks.difficulty: Open-ended research projects that took their authors about 270 days on average
benchmarks.paper_title: FrontierPhysics: Evaluating Agents for End-to-End Physics Research (arXiv, November 4, 2026)
benchmarks.authors: BenchFlow with physicists from UC Berkeley, Caltech, Harvard and other institutions

benchmarks.name: SkillsBench official leaderboard (BenchFlow)
benchmarks.description: BenchFlow's own SkillsBench table: each agent setup runs the 87 tasks of version 1.1 with Skills, the instruction folders an agent can load, and most also run them without.
benchmarks.format: Agent tasks run up to three times each, with Skills and, for most setups, without

benchmarks.name: MuirBench
benchmarks.description: A multi-image understanding benchmark of 2,600 multiple-choice questions across 11,264 images and 12 tasks, pairing every answerable question with a minimally altered unanswerable variant.
benchmarks.tasks: 2,600 pairwise multiple-choice questions across 11,264 images and 12 multi-image tasks
benchmarks.paper_title: MuirBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Robust Multi-image Understanding

benchmarks.name: GroundingME
benchmarks.description: A visual grounding benchmark of 1,005 examples that tests whether multimodal models localize objects across four dimensions: discriminative look-alikes, spatial relations, occluded or tiny targets, and ungroundable rejection queries.
benchmarks.difficulty: Fine-grained object localization and ungroundable rejection
benchmarks.paper_title: GroundingME: Exposing the Visual Grounding Gap in MLLMs through Multi-Dimensional Evaluation
benchmarks.authors: Li et al. (Peking University & Xiaomi, CVPR 2026)

benchmarks.name: BVB
benchmarks.description: A vision evaluation reported by Thinking Machines Lab under Vision Interpretation and Creation in the Inkling 2 Mini launch table and model card.
benchmarks.tasks: Vision interpretation and creation tasks (as reported by Thinking Machines Lab)

benchmarks.name: HoneyBench
benchmarks.description: A reward-hacking and specification-gaming safety benchmark from Goodhart Labs that pairs difficult agent tasks with exploitable graders to measure how often models cheat instead of solving the task honestly. Lower scores are better.
benchmarks.tasks: 20 private honeypot tasks across 7 domains with exploitable evaluators

benchmarks.name: Arena Agent
benchmarks.description: Arena ranks models by how they do in real Agent Mode sessions on arena.ai. Since November 18, 2026 the board is the Agent Capability Index, one score built from four session signals: task outcome, praise vs complaint, steering burden and bash reliability.
benchmarks.tasks: Real Agent Mode sessions on arena.ai
benchmarks.difficulty: Multi-step agent work chosen by users

benchmarks.name: Arena Agent net improvement
benchmarks.description: Arena's earlier Agent board, which ranked models by net improvement in real Agent Mode sessions, with confirmed success, praise vs complaint, steerability, bash recovery and tool hallucination beside it. Replaced by the Agent Capability Index on November 18, 2026.
benchmarks.tasks: Real Agent Mode sessions on arena.ai
benchmarks.difficulty: Multi-step agent work chosen by users

benchmarks.name: Intelligence per Watt
benchmarks.full_name: Intelligence per Watt (local AI energy efficiency)
benchmarks.description: A local-AI efficiency metric from Stanford Hazy Research Lab and Scaling Intelligence Lab measuring task accuracy delivered per joule of energy consumed per query on local hardware.
benchmarks.tasks: Local LLM query efficiency benchmark suite
benchmarks.paper_title: Intelligence per Watt: Measuring Intelligence Efficiency of Local AI
benchmarks.authors: Saad-Falcon, Narayan et al. (Stanford Hazy Research & Scaling Intelligence Lab)

benchmarks.name: CritPt v2 (Full)
benchmarks.description: The full research-level physics evaluation set in CritPt v2 (Complex Research using Integrated Thinking - Physics Test), covering unpublished graduate and frontier physics challenges with code execution.
benchmarks.tasks: Composite unpublished research-level physics challenges (Full set)

benchmarks.name: CritPt v2 (Hard)
benchmarks.description: The Hard subset of CritPt v2 isolating the most demanding multi-step unpublished physics research challenges.
benchmarks.tasks: Hard subset of CritPt v2 physics challenges

benchmarks.name: GraphWalks BFS 256K
benchmarks.description: Breadth-first-search graph traversal on the 256K-token context slice of GraphWalks, testing multi-hop reasoning over long contexts.
benchmarks.tasks: Multi-hop BFS graph traversal problems at 256K context
benchmarks.authors: OpenAI GraphWalks / Thinking Machines Lab (reported results)

benchmarks.name: FORTRESS (adversarial, Public)
benchmarks.description: The public adversarial split of Scale AI FORTRESS, measuring safe refusal and mitigation on high-risk adversarial safety prompts.
benchmarks.tasks: Public adversarial safety prompts from FORTRESS
benchmarks.authors: Scale AI FORTRESS / Thinking Machines Lab (reported results)

benchmarks.name: FORTRESS (benign, Public)
benchmarks.description: The public benign split of Scale AI FORTRESS, measuring whether a model answers harmless edge-case prompts without unnecessary refusal.
benchmarks.tasks: Public benign safety-adjacent prompts from FORTRESS
benchmarks.authors: Scale AI FORTRESS / Thinking Machines Lab (reported results)

benchmarks.name: Autoform-Hard
benchmarks.description: Vals AI benchmark that asks agents to complete Lean 4 formalizations of graduate- and research-level mathematics, graded by a clean-room proof checker.
benchmarks.format: Share of tasks whose proof passes clean-room grading
benchmarks.authors: Vals AI, on tasks from AutoformBench (Meta FAIR)

benchmarks.name: RollerCoasterTycoonBench
benchmarks.description: Vals AI benchmark in which decision models run a RollerCoaster Tycoon 2 theme park for three in-game years, one multiple-choice decision at a time.
benchmarks.tasks: 96 weekly turns in one park, three runs per model
benchmarks.format: Score from park growth and rating
benchmarks.difficulty: Sequential business decisions with delayed outcomes

benchmarks.name: Antidote
benchmarks.description: Surge AI's leaderboard of real everyday prompts graded by experts: doctors, lawyers and engineers read each answer in full, check its citations and run its code. Each model gets a rating with an interval.
benchmarks.difficulty: Everyday assistant use, judged for substance
benchmarks.paper_title: Antidote Leaderboard: Optimizing for Long-Term You

benchmarks.name: Hemingway-bench
benchmarks.description: Surge AI's writing leaderboard: professional writers judge creative, business and everyday writing for taste, originality, coherence and emotional intelligence. Each model gets a rating with an interval.
benchmarks.tasks: Creative, business and everyday writing tasks
benchmarks.difficulty: Writing quality as judged by professional writers

benchmarks.name: sudo L7
benchmarks.full_name: sudo L7: senior engineering judgment for coding agents (Surge AI)
benchmarks.description: Surge AI's coding-agent benchmark of 60 tasks written by professional software engineers. Agents must navigate unfamiliar systems, choose architectures, spot hidden risks and know when working code is still the wrong thing to ship.
benchmarks.tasks: 60 tasks written by professional software engineers
benchmarks.format: Agent runs graded against expert rubrics in eight dimensions

benchmarks.name: DAYJOB: Law
benchmarks.description: The legal track of Surge AI's DAYJOB: long legal assignments in contract review, due diligence, research memos, regulatory filings and litigation support, graded against expert rubrics.
benchmarks.tasks: Long legal assignments across five practice areas
benchmarks.format: Agent work products graded against attorney-written rubrics

benchmarks.name: DAYJOB: Tax
benchmarks.description: The tax track of Surge AI's DAYJOB: 50 professional tax assignments spanning 1,789 files, from individual returns to partnerships, estates and international taxation.
benchmarks.format: Agent work graded against expert rubrics at a 95% threshold

benchmarks.name: GDP.xlsx
benchmarks.description: Surge AI's spreadsheet benchmark: models work inside real workbooks such as financial models, lab results and engineering calculations, and must follow the evidence across sheets to an answer a professional could rely on.
benchmarks.format: Answers graded against must-have rubric criteria
benchmarks.paper_title: GDP.xlsx: Can Agents Understand the Spreadsheets That Run the World?

benchmarks.name: Chartography leaderboard (Surge AI)
benchmarks.description: Surge AI's own Chartography table: its run of every model on professional chart reading, from Kaplan-Meier curves to Bode plots.

benchmarks.name: ComplexConstraints leaderboard (Surge AI)
benchmarks.description: Surge AI's own ComplexConstraints table: its run of every model on professional prompts whose constraints interact, apply conditionally or must be inferred.

benchmarks.name: DAYJOB: Finance leaderboard (Surge AI)
benchmarks.description: Surge AI's own DAYJOB: Finance table: its run of every model on long finance assignments across corporate finance, banking, credit, investing and real assets.

benchmarks.name: DAYJOB: Healthcare leaderboard (Surge AI)
benchmarks.description: Surge AI's own DAYJOB: Healthcare table: its run of every model on long clinical, operational, payer, pharmacy and compliance assignments.

benchmarks.name: EnterpriseBench: CoreCraft leaderboard (Surge AI)
benchmarks.description: Surge AI's own EnterpriseBench table: its run of every model as an agent inside CoreCraft, a large simulated startup.

benchmarks.name: GDP.pdf leaderboard (Surge AI)
benchmarks.description: Surge AI's own GDP.pdf table: its run of every model on real professional prompts over PDFs from expert workflows.

benchmarks.name: HANDBOOK.md leaderboard (Surge AI)
benchmarks.description: Surge AI's own HANDBOOK.md table: its run of every model as an agent that must follow a long company handbook across five enterprise domains.

benchmarks.name: Riemann-bench leaderboard (Surge AI)
benchmarks.description: Surge AI's own Riemann-bench table: its run of every model on research-level mathematics problems written by mathematicians.
